behavioral_notes.observation: rating.rating is the satisfaction fact: a Float 'rating' value constrained 0-5 by the _rating_range SQL check, mapped to grades great/okay/bad (>=4 / >=3 / <3) and text top/ok/ko via rating_data. It carries a res_model/res_id Many2oneReference to ANY rated record (generic, polymorphic), a uuid access_token (_default_access_token) for the public email flow, a 'consumed' flag separating sent-but-unanswered from filled ratings, and an optional message_id link so a chatter mail.message can render the rating. create()/write() auto-stamp rated_on and resolve parent_res_model/parent_res_id via _find_parent_data. Not visible in metadata.

The rating.mixin behaviour lives on the mail.thread extension. rating_send_request(template) posts a mail.template (mt_note) to the customer carrying a /rate/<token> link minted by _rating_get_access_token (reuses an unconsumed rating or creates one as sudo). rating_apply(rate, token=...) writes rating+feedback+consumed=True on the rating.rating and, if the record is a mail.thread, posts/updates a chatter message embedding the rating image; notify_delay_send schedules the mail +2h so the rater can still edit. This is the closed loop survey->store->chatter, none of it readable from metadata.

Two public (auth='public', website=True) HTTP routes implement the customer-facing survey. _get_rating_and_record resolves the rating.rating by access_token as sudo (404 if missing); a non-public logged-in user whose commercial partner differs from rating.partner_id is rejected (rating_external_page_invalid_partner). submit_feedback (POST) validates rate in {1,3,5} (UNHAPPY/NEUTRAL/HAPPY) and calls record_sudo.rating_apply, then renders the thank-you page. The public->sudo escalation after token+partner check is the security boundary and is invisible to metadata.

rating_avg and rating_count are computed together in one _read_group over consumed ratings with rating>=1 (RATING_LIMIT_MIN); rating_percentage_satisfaction = great*100/total (or -1 when none), where 'great' = rating>=4. rating_last_value is fetched via raw SQL array_agg ordered by write_date for performance. rating.parent.mixin rolls the same satisfaction % up to a parent record (e.g. project from its tasks) over parent_res_id, optionally windowed by _rating_satisfaction_days. Compute formulas live in Python, not metadata.

3 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 1 patch (Message.prototype via core/common/message_model_patch.js) plus a notification_item patch; bundles include mail.assets_public and portal.assets_chatter so the rating renders inside the discuss/portal chatter, not a standalone app.

classification.rationale: rating is a cross-cutting customer-satisfaction/feedback backbone, not a primary value-creating activity. Like mail.thread, it ships two abstract mixins (rating.mixin, rating.parent.mixin) plus a generic polymorphic fact model (rating.rating, res_model/res_id to ANY record) that many primary modules graft onto — project, helpdesk, website_slides, event, im_livechat, website_sale — to measure satisfaction of their own deliverables. Under Stabell & Fjeldstad it is firm-infrastructure SUPPORT: it creates no order/delivery/invoice of its own; it instruments others. APQC 6.0 Manage Customer Service captures the satisfaction-measurement intent (the surrounding chatter/customer-inquiry handling is mapped support under mail in apqc_odoo_map.tsv).

standard_capabilities: rating stored as chatter message with star/smiley image
satisfaction analytics: avg, count, % satisfaction, repartition (pivot/graph)
reusable mixin grafted onto any mail.thread model
typical_fits: satisfaction % shown on the rated record and rolled up to its parent
common_gaps: rating scale beyond the fixed 0-5 / happy-neutral-unhappy mapping
multi-question or NPS-style surveys (rating stores a single value + feedback)
custom satisfaction thresholds / grade boundaries (great/okay/bad hardcoded in rating_data)
non-email rating channels (SMS/in-app) beyond the provided web route
